title: Fish Pie
subtitle: Classic British fish in cream sauce under mashed potato
excerpt: The quintessential British fish pie: salmon, smoked haddock, and prawns in a creamy, parsley-rich sauce under a deep mashed potato crust, baked until golden. Comforting, elegant, and one of those dishes that tastes better than the sum of its parts.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fish pie is a traditional British dish with roots in the medieval tradition of fish days (when meat was prohibited by religious observance and fish was eaten instead). The modern version, with its cream sauce and mashed potato topping, was established in the twentieth century as a comfort food staple. The best fish pies use a combination of fish: white fish for texture, smoked fish for depth, and shellfish for luxury. The sauce is a velouté (stock and cream-enriched béchamel) made with the milk used to poach the fish, which concentrates the fish flavour. Boiled eggs are a traditional addition in many classic recipes, adding richness and protein. The potato topping should be piped or forked to create ridges that brown in the oven.

content.text: Gently poach the fish in the milk rather than boiling; boiling makes it tough and releases too much water. Make the sauce with the poaching milk; this is where all the flavour is. The filling must be fully cooled before the mash goes on top; hot filling will cause the mash to sink into it. Assemble and refrigerate overnight for the best results.

items.preparation: skinless undyed; cut into large chunks
600ml for poaching the fish; 100ml for the mash
50g for the sauce; 30g for the mash
peeled; cut into chunks; for the mash

content.text: Gently poach the salmon and haddock in the milk over the lowest heat for 5 minutes until just cooked. Remove the fish. Reserve the poaching milk. Make a béchamel: melt 50g butter, add flour, cook for 1 minute, then gradually add the poaching milk and cream. Stir until thick and smooth. Season and fold in the parsley.
Flake the poached fish into large pieces into a baking dish. Add the raw prawns and quartered hard-boiled eggs. Pour the sauce over evenly. Leave to cool.

Boil the potatoes until tender. Drain and mash with the remaining butter and 100 ml milk until smooth. Season well. Spread or pipe the mash over the cooled fish in an even layer, using a fork to create ridges. Heat the oven to 190°C / fan 170°C / gas 5. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden on top and bubbling at the edges.
